current.text: He is expected to start for Golden State. Steve Kerr likes him.
His minutes are expected to rise to 30 or more per game, with about 20% usage.
Jimmy Butler is out for at least half the season. Moses Moody is out at the start of the season.
Experts expect a step up and a likely top 100 season, with gains in threes, rebounds, steals, assists and points.
With Butler out, he could handle the ball more and have a strong early run of assists. His potential assist conversion was only 47%.
He finished 136th last season in limited minutes, but ranked 61st after the All-Star break, when he played about 32 minutes per game.
His role looks secure on a thin roster that struggles to field a 10-man rotation. He does not have to adjust to a new team.
His ESPN rank (66 to 74) is too high. Around pick 90 to 100 is fine.
At his Yahoo and Fantrax price (around 116 to 120) he is good value, more so in category leagues. He is called the best Warriors target and a bit underrated, a good last round pick.
He should start the season well, but Warriors players are expected to fade as the season goes on.
He would gain value if Steph Curry gets hurt.
The Warriors' schedule is good for a playoff ending March 28, but they have 15 back-to-backs, tied for second most.

durable.text: He sometimes has efficiency problems and lacks defense.
He tends to start seasons slowly and has struggled in the playoffs.
He rebounds well for a guard. No category is a league outlier and none is weak for his position.

note: He is a cheap late auction pick: Yahoo values him at 4 USD (average cost 1.0, rank 105) and ESPN at 6 USD (rank 69). The experts like him at the Yahoo price and call ESPN's top 70 rank too high. His balanced line (5.5 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 1.1 steals, no weak category) fits any build as a 1 to 4 USD guard. Early on, check that he starts and plays 30 or more minutes while Butler is out, and think about selling before Butler returns and the Warriors fade.
